# Robin Hood The Legend of Sherwood; 2002 Stealth Strategy Game

Published: 2014-02-26T14:45:00.001-08:00
URL: https://tactdb.blogspot.com/2014/02/robin-hood-legend-of-sherwood-2002.html

[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjPNnjIUU6v3udbdikpw9mq9EEU4zrIUECrEgHvNi5O9QOlUqqZZD_gD5NdIFj89x99c_DN57iqYzcXHngfj8FrPm4npVIG7WewwHbhtTzbAhZC0_y36l7RtyMiWGAy0jGxekIFyRauiET7/s1600/title.jpg)

  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj6DDywN_y6cfxsa2f1xrxTFPfGzrrcmvJtDnk0Z-9smqH5JftwL_8LPqa_hy2X-9HQpz4HrprZsTi-nYGztsmOP4KFQOlhU7q4SRi-48au2hC5L4_0qTLBJr8MtWm_aRBwYmN6_eU6RC_d/s1600/castle.jpg)  
---  
Lincoln Castle  
  
  
I have to give a nod to this game.  During a time when publishers were releasing stealth-based isometric squad-based games, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood took it to a much more artistic and thematic level in a successful attempt to stand out from the rest of the market.  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiL_uLuG_PtYlvsav2EKriZNC2LYtlriQQbBKjXzRSYMJslwLbSEghCjiHtYgAcyI9xkv135bmEr4liNFleBRtU26uY4VUu1vPnofsPdQMI1DfYjDnVpDVLHtM0KCyP1Guw6sRHFmhrXmDf/s1600/buildingcutout.jpg)  
---  
A lot of cutouts are featured in Robin Hood The Legend of Sherwood  
  
  
  
Robinhood comes back to Sherwood after spending years fighting in one of the Crusades (how noble....) and finds the rotten Sheriff of Nottingham to have subjected the people to cruel and unusual punishment, including Robins own father and his beloved Marian.  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEikmelAQBBdwuxjojcdg8UNNefUpRW75dJLHrdQe0t_nyHh0Q7Yfr_dYMpdy7jXbAnGdSxE7JyThy1Mr4m-8p41MvlEdm8vQsr3jRJ9XcSXbwIshL8vFo5BuhbFInl_lmhHNIGlE_BWQLE8/s1600/defendrobin.gif)  
---  
Four merry men shielding Robin using their Shield ability.  
Notice how they keep their backs to Robin and face a  
single direction.  
The game is quite appealing in a thematic and visual sense.  Robin Hood himself is endowed with three skills.  One is to shoot an arrow which usually kills anyone in a single hit (some armored opponents need multiple arrows and soldiers who have spotted Robin Hood and carry a shield can deflect arrow attacks).  Another skill is to throw a money bag.  Money bags, like arrows, are an ammunition and must be found or crafted by your merry men.   Money bags are great at distracting civilians and lesser soldiers.  However disciplined soldiers, officers, and other special personnel are immune to the enticement of gold.  The final skill Robin Hood has at his disposal is your good old fashioned Punch which literally is the donkey-punch used in  knocking out unaware individuals.  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgURm1ki45xQPeBjxrCpCUzWJEkbiLIl_AuBiqw8CNQOAvcnFmmpvisHJCFhOGb4Lf0kwNRfyE9PkcpTdhQnZ8qX_bcU-a3yi35J7vOuHxqyTD9IRqWC0dCUqjr91hBtYxV39Fi2kViPxwW/s1600/swordfight.jpg)  
---  
Using the mouse to make a quick _'C'_ to counter the enemies   
thrust.  
The game mechanics themselves were unique, characters at times would need to battle other soldiers in a sword fight.  The player would have to draw patterns, like an 'S', an 'L' and other connecting shapes and lines to deflect, thrust, flank attack, and commit to all forms of combat actions.  Considering the age of the game (2002) that was an amazing thing to experience, the harder the game difficulty was, the faster and trickier the AI was.  This allowed players with skill to overcome their lack of stealth or strategic planning; do not take this as some sort of free-pass.  Combat in _Robin Hood_ was intense, difficult, and characters lacked any armor or protection which meant death was quite easy.  A player could easily find his characters swarmed or defeated by 2-3 blows.  It did however add a sense of daring and bravado when attacking heavily armored enemies in feint assaults.   
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
Combat-oriented characters were important in creating distractions, and utilizing the combat mechanics, characters such as Little John with his staff can run into a crowd, spin by drawing an 'O' knocking most soldiers on their feet, and run away while Robin Hood sneaks inside.   Blunt weapons would stun enemies as opposed to killing them, maintaining your non-lethal secondary objective of limiting causalities (such as clubs and flails).  There was a downside to killing enemy soldiers and that it detracted people from joining your cause; that translated to less merry men to craft, set up ambushes and aid in combat (more on that later).   
  
  
  
  
Robin Hood didn't act alone.  A wave of merry men in all shapes and forms supported him.  There were three archtype merry men henchmen that could help Robin Hood in any storyline quests, or even commit to ambush, defense, and offensive missions on their own whilst Robin heals at Sherwood Forest.  These henchmen break up as follows (these names are what I've called them; I don't remember their official names):  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjrFcUU_8Ox3eqmiIH19xxrgpaeajOMkQ9ot99ciXsCarspun1deVNP3XanSSM9LHaRh29KRMoccZP13u3B1qcVUS2Sds6DyacqxYvQgus5D4lR4bytRIW3DWNIb-YATW9_6aC2hKUXe1yZ/s1600/henchmen.jpg)  
---  
Archer, Pikemen, and Muscle respectively.  
  
  


  * The Archer; Can fire arrows like Robin,  can use his shield to defend others whilst facing a certain direction and tie-up anyone who is stunned or knocked down.  Uses a sword in combat.
  * The Pikemen; Can throw apples (apples distract guards, if there are kids nearby they chase the kids who run far and fast), can heal others with herbs, and pitchfork and kill anyone who is knocked out or stunned. Uses a pitchfork in combat.  Has the ability to pick-lock doors.
  * The Muscle; Can whistle to attract attention, can eat a leg of meat to heal himself, and can pick up and drop bodies.  Uses a club in combat.

  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh47SssjvaurZVUg9DqVAzX9cAI7OIKBVhBd72DLUo46GK9MIDVtLqL5-KeFMeBFtmo3j3K3dHv2xE7o5hYzm7urnpmtutSkYu2AdI5i7yjfeRhdUmZixkuZPjJixzULULnu5834vQS7RVs/s1600/maid.jpg)Five other regular characters are recruited along the way and act like heroes.  These characters had special abilities, much higher starting stats and could be revived by fellow merry men if players had clovers.  Clovers were lives in-game.  Should Robin Hood or one of the other main merry men get defeated by an enemy (ie zero health points) they can be revived through one of these clovers.  However this does not work on regular merry me and should a main hero die without a clover than the game is over.   
  
  
  
  
  
  


[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhrdXZoGudD0spcDws16Aff95eaMwgaXwvdxXCHr4uTslPnenuVRmRsgTWsyc4IAeseHZqmC9NR6JPUG8I4PL1SDVUJSLRYzLehxC2teRH-3vxj8RjlqS_uYyzqE2GAjPfbZyVlBUVxdnRd/s1600/regularheroes.jpg)

  
  


  * Stuteley; Can throw nets (which incapacitate groups of opponents), can punch like Robin, and can disguise himself as a beggar to scout or to hide.  Is armed with an Axe and can pick-lock doors.
  * Will Scarlet; Can shoot slingshots which is an effective short range 1-hit knock out ability, he can also strangle enemies (silently kill them) and can shield others.  He is armed with a flail, a heavy blunt weapon.
  * Little John;  Can whistle for distraction, can also stun punch enemies, and can offer the Leg Up skill which allows Little John to boost any merry man to the second floor of any surface (such as small houses, over certain walls, and so on).  Little John is armed with a blunt staff, useful in taking on multiple enemies.  He can also move bodies and corpses.
  * Maid Marian; She can fire an arrow, heal other characters with herbs and her unique skill is to spy which reveals all units within a screen-sized radius.  She is armed with a sword.
  * Friar Tuck; This character has the most useful skills.  He can throw a bee hive which releases bees, stinging and distracting large groups of guards.  He can also lay down a drinking pouch filled with mead.  Soldiers (and even some lone sergeants) can fall prey to their own addictions and drink till they pass out or leave their patrol route to enjoy themselves.  The final skill for Friar Tuck is to eat a leg of meat to heal himself.  He is armed with a Mace, a blunt weapon.

  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjUIKKYhfToigp3yPoQu9c3yYrqxOaWzcJqgcLaknZaPr5LJicXv7sevtSFNkgxOMdlaQBZTx7bn-TNLH98rwy36jG6yzBRzTvreuQwF3DMonDUAXsQuHvPoBXxvEdDJrMS9XFOZVDS0f4c/s1600/sgtorders.jpg)  
---  
A sergeant issuing out orders.  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg2oydY0r_FTILeTDxrAOAqpwdo4TSU9bnrVC2qV2BlGzIIT2O7VIc0NDAKbMfHzW21rmY9j-n3pbtRgEbK766D61s_uSv2w4-rQeHQoSNZaeDhdcOGLd8rSCgR6Avg4Hghax1VVu7xKiaM/s1600/sgtunit.jpg)  
---  
A patrol commanded by a  
sergeant.  
The AI was also quite accurate to the games theme.  There were sergeants who commanded small units of soldiers.  Whenever a soldier saw something out of line he would run to a sergeant first, giving player some time, if skillful, to intercept the runner.  If the runner succeeds in reaching a sergeant then the sergeant will rally reinforcements to accompany him in his investigation.  Sergeants reinforce discipline, which means soldiers would not break formation or guard duty to collect coins should Robin try to distract them with a money purse.  The sergeant himself is quite disciplined and is considerably more stronger than his subordinate soldier.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg2GoKio_ULkP_1_x93Q956Rm-JVywRF7zd55iy7eUOmNjH6Zu_civKYIHFmMKzNe1Q32in03ruVsRbWS1H9YFWab6L5zHvJFCWUqNNP7Fm6aVLLVcoQ_V4MS5GqZFWlW9fhEvn1FruU4nk/s1600/archers2.jpg)  
---  
Left: Shield formation set up | Right: Archers firing from cover  
Soldiers also work in tangent with one another in a combined arms effort.  Infantry cover archers with their shields whilst knights and mounted units go straight for the kill.  Pikemen try to go for the flanks while sergeants try to take an over watch position or continue to issue orders, such as sending a runner to retrieve reinforcements from another part of the map.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
Civilians also play their own role.  Children are usually just awed at Robin Hood whilst the ladies will be wooed by him.  However if Robin has been notoriously killing soldiers and civilians then civilians will run in panic at the sight of Robin, most times straight to soldiers.  Civilians will also alert soldiers whenever they spot a body or anything foul.  Soldiers may or may not listen to civilians.  Sergeants also have a tendency not to listen to civilians, but will almost always listen to soldiers.  It should be noted however higher-tiered units seem to reduce the chance of ignoring civilian reports.  If certain civilians report foul-play (such as spotting a body) only to come investigate and find no corpse (because it was removed by one of Robins merry men) then confidence in civilian reporting goes down.  This can be used to great a series of false-alarms to make civilian reporting impotent.  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhkG5jc2lL0cPgaLBKC7tolqnqaTs7s7uqvEfUkwNoibnNnKHu7SEMbSxw9AkAsTJMhDKmvMOpSFvJQaSlgQLgH63PDYJHFSMekXisxFuIiOlgNo7J0G2W5iWKE5FIE2RTXHX_UPpiKoAtH/s1600/sherwood.jpg)  
---  
Sherwood forest where the merry men gather to regroup.  Various crafting tables and huts are visible.  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgBCkjQSmNb2VPgFCohe8HlkM4PWFUUMxJuJwORRAEkoDu8EEypivwU24PXPrdhAMhz-s9FZ1MGQYYmiMPDZcTwKbUchHCnr0WsYqHTeQTGnjJiybe8klEVPt0X79eWPObxWJ8TiX8t6fGc/s1600/missionmap.jpg)  
---  
Mission map showing castles and  
crossroads.  Buttons light up when  
missions are available.  
After every mission Robin Hood and his gang return back to their HQ in Sherwood forest.  This base of operations has several tables and huts which, once manned, can be used to create items such as arrows, nets and other expendable skill items.  There are also areas where merry men can heal or train for better combat statistics (such as damage and HP).  In Sherwood the player can open up a smaller mission map in the corner to see what viable missions are there.  Missions are broken down into main quests, ambush missions, offensive missions, and defensive missions.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgZJOTZz-jQJEKK8jwuwQHKSMfPgeuLKtxYcE3-3tKlC_fPSOP2V4bW7ODYC6iXulBejI8SexANzHWflTSOciZDJKrwi6w72mBoYAI1Iin0AxkHpCxljTgFHCKy35MUwmeCVKbKx9K0dIn3/s1600/pulltrap.gif)  
---  
Springing a net-trap on a tax-collector and his escort.  
Main missions are self-explanatory and usually revolve around a castle or a keep and its surrounding village.  They are the main mechanism in telling the story of Robin Hood The Legend of Sherwood.  The other missions are more economic in nature, allowing you to steal money or acquire new recruits.  Offensive missions tend to be attacks against small bands of soldiers who may be patrolling around Sherwood.  Defensive missions are calls for help from small villages being harassed by the Sheriffs men.  However the most interesting and entertaining missions are the ambush ones designed to steal money from one of the Sheriffs gold convoys.  This will be at times a simple tax collector on foot or a whole horse carriage (which is usually struck from the side with a large log).  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhus69br00zbDTK_92rWE9vj9ln8oNpnINiAqsYAWomFpVYEJ2n0m7BpmQZB6FX-SpdYjrzQfFs6OlvfgcQNsOhuhRoRmaBFm_sipFaS5Eb8AfuS114U3tRhVX4Zy2gjHCH3KiqaVtlG_or/s1600/robinluremanhole.gif)  
---  
Robin luring two soldiers to manhole traps.  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjB8u7qK0uEGjOap-O5k8fPEchm-XyDJI2UoyRV97DUiMAgr7-i59Dt-yCUM_dWYohZyn2ugmo7rO6ijeco9iJhazIqU5VOJBSSSRZu5enM7dCoUob3mOG9C4fy56cCt4zF6tdc7ieAKFqF/s1600/traparchers.jpg)  
---  
Robin fires an arrow on target to   
reveal the hidden archers behind the   
bush.  
These ambush missions are very clever and tend to have multiple traps laid around.  These traps encompass simple manholes to hidden merry men such as archers or men armed with staffs (great for pre-occupying enemies without killing them).  There are also net traps and other clever techniques that help Robin and his gang rob the Sheriffs gold carriage.  These missions could be launched with only regular merry men as opposed to main-quest missions which required Robin to attend regardless of his status.  The objective is to steal gold so knocking out every soldier is unnecessary and most of the time bold maneuvers such as a distraction followed by a snatch-and-grab tend to be more feasible than attempting to take on the various formations of infantry units (which, in later parts of the game, becomes more and more competent in covering each other).  
  
  
  
  
  
  
[](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhWc6Rb9WUcOmv9JSrXSbpwZcrJuQnd3wM4fvQPuOmAzfzMkH38E_fOtQ1XYb3wjyYLmI1aH-Z20h95hd-XN4pvfIsq1lvuZjhlAnlh8RQKx-BrAvH6B99mdjH7uiJTqGTnMOOa_738TbSr/s1600/sideram.gif)  
---  
A log-ram striking the side of a carriage alerting all guards.  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
The main-quest missions were long and intricate but their objectives were quite simple.  Make contact with this person, or release this person from prison.  There are even missions where killing any enemy soldiers will automatically end the game as its part of a prerequiste for mission completion.

King John and his escort of heavily armored, broad-sword wielding Knights
